## v2.5.9 Release notes

> QQ Group: 1002583295

This release adds quick routing actions, live rule updates, persistent FakeIP caching, TUN stack selection, and daily startup-warning dismissal. It also redesigns global notifications and improves automatic startup, installation, updates, and long-running reliability.

### Active connections and routing rules

- Added a context menu to active connections for creating process, domain, or IP rules. Connection details and the current egress policy are filled in automatically, with an option to choose another egress before saving.
- Rules are checked for duplicates and conflicts before saving. Existing identical rules are not duplicated; changing the egress replaces only the matching rule and preserves other rules. The menu also supports the keyboard menu key and Shift + F10.
- TUN routing now uses local rule sets that reload automatically after saving, without restarting aggregation. Existing connections keep their current path; new connections use the updated rules.
- Updated the routing page and quick-add dialog to explain live updates, replacing the previous restart-required warning.

### TUN and proxy modes

- Enabled persistent sing-box caching by default, storing domain-to-virtual-IP mappings when FakeIP is in use. TUN restarts and IPv4 fallback reuse the same cache to improve mapping continuity.
- Added TUN stack selection under Settings → Advanced network: `system`, `mixed` (system TCP + gVisor UDP), and `gvisor` (a full userspace stack). The default remains `system`; changes apply the next time TUN starts.
- Added a system-proxy takeover switch. When disabled, HypoMux provides local SOCKS5 and HTTP/HTTPS proxy ports without changing Windows system proxy settings, allowing manual application setup or use alongside other proxy tools. Automatic takeover remains the default.

### Notifications and interaction

- Fixed the release-notes dialog jumping down after checking for updates. It now starts at the top on both initial and subsequent opens for natural top-to-bottom reading.
- Redesigned global notifications as a Dynamic Island-style surface for saved settings, acceleration start/stop events, link changes, diagnostic results, and failures, reducing scattered feedback across pages.
- Repeated notifications are grouped with an occurrence count. Notifications support expanded details, dismissal, and retry actions where available; errors include clearer summaries and error codes.
- Improved light/dark theme integration and frosted-glass rendering, fixing ineffective background blur and mismatched surface colors.
- Added “Don't remind me again today” to startup risk prompts. Check it and choose Continue to keep advisory prompts hidden for the local calendar day, including after restarting the app. Reminders return the next day; startup checks and blocking errors remain enabled.
- Improved diagnostic feedback and page-state handling to avoid covering controls, unnecessary reloads after language changes, and stale updates after leaving a page.
- Added an official website button to About and linked [hypomux.com](https://hypomux.com) in the project documentation.

### Stability and compatibility

- Fixed automatic acceleration failing when selected adapters had not yet been enumerated during Windows startup. HypoMux now waits for them to appear within a bounded time before starting.
- Fixed races between Core startup, stop, and shutdown. Improved cleanup of background tasks, event listeners, and communication resources during repeated starts and exits.
- Fixed abnormal active-connection counts caused by repeated connection cleanup, and improved concurrent DNS-status access.
- Improved cancellation and timeout handling in network diagnostics and corrected probe accounting. SOCKS5 UDP now accepts IPv4-mapped addresses carried in IPv6 format.
- Reduced settings-save blocking caused by slow registry queries. Appearance-save failures now produce visible feedback, and failed cleanup of expired domain-isolation records preserves consistency between memory and storage.
- Improved Windows-version detection in the installer to avoid false rejections caused by compatibility-version reporting, while retaining architecture checks.
- Fixed upgrade checks treating harmless read-only access, such as security-software scans, as a locked Core executable. Failures now distinguish processes that remain running from genuine write locks.
- Hardened installer-path validation for automatic updates by rejecting special characters that could be misinterpreted by the command interpreter.

### Dependencies and maintenance

- Fixed dialog focus timing in quick-add routing tests and added regression coverage for the release-notes dialog's initial position and repeated opening.
- Upgraded sing-box from 1.13.19 to 1.13.21, retaining gVisor support and adding TUN DNS-configuration compatibility handling for later versions.
- Added regression coverage for live rule updates, FakeIP recovery after restart, stack selection, daily warning dismissal, and Core lifecycle behavior. Removed obsolete qualification scripts.
- Added English release notes for earlier versions to support bilingual website changelogs.

### Upgrade notes

- Supports Windows 10/11 x64. Install the official signed package over an existing installation; the installer safely stops HypoMux and the independent Core service before replacing files.
- After upgrading and restarting TUN, subsequent routing-rule changes reload automatically. Changing the TUN stack still requires a TUN restart.
- FakeIP mappings are stored in `cache/sing-box.db` under the configuration directory. Newly allocated mappings that have not yet been written may still be lost on forced termination. Remote rule subscriptions and automatic rule-pack updates are not included in this release.
- GitHub Releases and Tencent CNB Release continue to distribute the same SignPath-signed installer. Automatic updates still verify the Ed25519 manifest, file size, SHA-256, and Windows Authenticode signature.

> Thanks to SignPath.io for providing Windows code-signing services for HypoMux, and to SignPath Foundation for issuing the project's open-source code-signing certificate.
